d:
Ansirem has told me much of the elemental lords and I am afraid that we have good reason to fear Al'Akir now that the wards that have hidden Zephras are down. If the Windlord chooses to attack us, we stand no chance to defend ourselves while we are here in his domain.
High Elder Shadowsong needs to know of the danger we are in, and more importantly, what our intentions are for our mission to Azeroth. We will find the means to save our home. I swear it.
c:
Talaanis Shadowsong listens intently as you tell him of what transpired above the Shrine of Akir, and of Elaadrin's plan to leave Zephras Isle.
I need to reflect on this further, but looking at the upside, we have rid ourselves of Lorthuna and deprived the cult of their leader. Our home has not been invaded yet, and on the timeline of elemental demigods, it could be years... Decades even, before Al'Akir deigns to turn his attention to us.
There is much to fear now, but much to celebrate as well.

d:
Aye, the time's come, young adventurer. Ye've grown stout and sturdy, like the stone beneath our boots. Takin' up the adventurer's path shows ye've got the wisdom o' the mountain, even before ye've proven yerself. Ye've the grit of stone to walk the earth's path.
But to earn its favor, ye must face it proper. South o' here, the Frostmane trolls live in a cave.
Bring me two of the necklaces they wear, crafted from the Iceclaw bears. Then we'll speak more of yer future.
p:
Patience, lad, is the earth's finest virtue. It's seen mountains crumble and rivers carve valleys--slow and stubborn, like a true traveler. The earth calls to ye now, for trouble brews on the horizon. Return successful, and ye'll be one step closer to bein' whole.
Others may envy yer wisdom, but that's their burden to bear.
c:
Well done, lad. Ye've proven yerself ready. Earth's the bedrock of all things. It'll shield ye, but only if ye show it proper respect. Even stone can shift if slighted. Learn its ways, and ye'll grow wiser than most. Never forget the secrets it shares.
I'll craft ye a sapta now--accept it, and ye'll walk the true path.

d:
Aye, sapta's a brew forged with magic, bindin' our spirit to the elements. Only a few adventurer know the recipe, and it's nae for the weak-willed. Drink it, and ye will see what others can't. Hold true--it's only to be drunk in a sacred place.
Head north to the Spirit Stone, tucked at the end of a hidden path up the mountain. Drink it there... See what the earth has to show ye.
c:
Ah... Friend... The earth welcomes you, even in this frozen land. Bound in body and spirit, you'll walk forward knowing the mountains are your strength, the plains your patience, and the world your essence.
To pass this rite, stand humbly before the earth. The other elements are not so still--they clash and roar. Learn their dual nature, even here among the snow and stone.

d:
Take this rough quartz from me and bring it to Teo Hammerstorm as proof o' our meeting. He will craft a totem for ye, and this pebble will be the heart o' it. As small as it may seem, ye will come to find that size does not matter, and that even the smallest o' things can outlast many others.
Be patient, friend. Remain strong. And seek wisdom. This is what earth asks o' ye. In the end, ye shall become one with the earth--respect it as it shall respect ye.
p: Ahh, ye've returned. If ye have the stone, it means the mountain's chosen ye true. I'll give ye the totem it promised. But if ye've come empty-handed, off with ye! The path ain't for those who forget their way.
c: Well done! Know this--totems ain't just a mark of yer place among adventurers. They're tools, a focus for spells tied to stone, soil, and other elements. As ye grow wiser, more o' the mountain's power will open to ye. The trainers will know when yer ready for more. But for now, take this totem, and let the ground speak through ye.
